description: A fictional short-burn jetpack game prop for a demolition engineer, chunky low-poly, shown alone with no person. One thick charcoal back frame plate behind two upright fat ochre painted fuel cylinders mounted side by side, each with a wide chamfered domed top carrying a small charcoal cap, a tapering bottom, and exactly two wide charcoal bands round it. Between the cylinders one boxy ochre valve block with one small teal lamp window in a thick charcoal bezel on its face. Under each cylinder one thick dark steel bell nozzle pointing straight down on a short charcoal neck. On top of the frame between the cylinders one thick charcoal arched grab handle. On the wearer-side face behind the frame two fat padded charcoal shoulder straps rise from the frame's top edge and loop backward and down, and one wide charcoal waist strap with a big rectangular buckle runs round the lower part. No flame.
proportions: About 0.37 m long front to back, 0.41 m wide and 0.58 m tall. (length : width : height = 0.90 : 1 : 1.41)
sides: the pack is symmetric about its centre plane (x = 0): the valve block with its teal lamp window is on that plane on the front face, the two cylinders and the two nozzles are mirror images, the two shoulder straps are mirror images. Frame words: the pack's FRONT is the big OUTER face with the two cylinders; its REAR is the wearer side (the back of the charcoal frame with the shoulder straps and the waist strap); its LEFT and RIGHT flanks are the two narrow width ends.
